question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsech}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\operatorname{arsech}⁡({3}^{x})] \\  & =-\frac{1}{{3}^{x}\sqrt{1-{({3}^{x})}^{2}}}\cdot {({3}^{x})}^{′} \\  & =-\frac{1}{{3}^{x}\sqrt{1-{9}^{x}}}\cdot {3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{\sqrt{1-{9}^{x}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
